name: Advanced Taxiways
description:
[h1]Advanced Taxiways[/h1]
Stops aircraft deadlocking on taxiways, and stops them waiting for traffic that is nowhere near them.

[b]The problems[/b]
An aircraft reserves its entire route the moment it is plotted, then sits at its stand for up to three minutes waiting for a pushback truck. Everything crossing that route queues behind an aeroplane that has not moved - most visibly an arrival that stops dead at the runway exit just after landing.

Aircraft also wait for traffic on the far side of the airport, because precedence is decided by whoever plotted a route first rather than by who is actually there. And two aircraft meeting head-on in a single-lane taxiway or ramp connector simply stop, because neither can reverse.

[b]What it does[/b]
[list]
[*]A waiting aircraft reserves only the ground it stands on and pushes back into, and claims the rest when it starts rolling.
[*]An aircraft blocked by one that is nowhere near the node they are arguing over can take its turn back. The game has this and it only works when exactly one aircraft is ahead of you.
[*]Single-lane stretches are worked out from your taxiway layout and cleared one direction at a time, like a controller clearing a segment to a hold-short point. Opposing traffic waits outside instead of meeting half way.
[*]Departures are held at the stand when the only way out is contested, rather than reversing into it. Waiting at a stand costs nothing; a blocked connector stops everything.
[*]When two aircraft reach a node together, precedence follows the ladder the game already uses for its runway queue - emergency, then anything clearing a runway, then general aviation last.
[*]Any deadlock that still forms is detected and broken.
[/list]

[b]Notes[/b]
Nothing is written into your saves - removing the mod leaves no trace. Every rule can be switched off individually in Configuration Manager (F1), and the tuning values are exposed there too.

Built entirely out of machinery the game already has and either never calls or calls too narrowly.
author: Rhamnos
